JSON: Name: fmri_to_musiclm_pipeline Title: A pipeline combining fMRI-to-embedding regression and MusicLM-conditioned synthesis to reconstruct and localize high-level musical semantics from auditory-cortex activity Short Hypothesis: Accurate prediction of MuLan music embeddings from auditory-cortex fMRI causes MusicLM-conditioned reconstructions to match the original stimuli on high-level semantic similarity (genre, instrumentation, mood) significantly better than reconstructions conditioned on predicted non-music embeddings or random retrieval. Related Work: Prior work on brain–audio correspondences has used encoding models to map audio-derived features (melspectrograms, self-supervised speech embeddings, CNN-derived music features) to fMRI responses and decoding efforts to reconstruct low-level spectrotemporal content from brain activity. Separately, text-to-music generative systems and joint text+audio embedding models enable high-fidelity conditional audio synthesis and produce compact semantic representations. Existing brain-decoding studies either focus on low-level acoustic reconstruction or on classification of musical attributes with handcrafted or task-agnostic features; they do not exploit music-specialized joint embeddings for generation. Limitations in current methods include reliance on non-music-trained embeddings, weak alignment between temporally coarse fMRI and high-resolution audio embeddings, constrained retrieval-based decoding by dataset size, limited evaluation of semantic fidelity in generated audio, and mixed evidence on whether linear mappings sufficiently capture brain-to-embedding correspondences. Abstract: We propose an end-to-end research pipeline that tests whether high-level musical semantics encoded by a music-specialized joint embedding (MuLan) can be predicted from human auditory-cortex fMRI and used to condition a text-to-music generative model (MusicLM) to reconstruct perceived music. The pipeline integrates voxel-wise fMRI-to-embedding regression, retrieval baselines from an expansive music corpus, MusicLM-conditioned synthesis, and whole-brain encoding analyses to localize representations. Main contributions are (1) a rigorous experimental protocol comparing music-specialized versus non-music embeddings as decoding targets, (2) paired retrieval and generative evaluations quantifying semantic fidelity using embedding similarity, classifier-based semantic agreement, and human perceptual ratings, and (3) encoding results mapping unique variance of text- and audio-derived embeddings across auditory cortex. Expected outcomes are empirical quantification of how much high-level musical semantics are accessible from fMRI, an assessment of generation fidelity when conditioning on predicted embeddings, and a spatial profile of semantic representation in the auditory cortex. Experiments: Datasets: (1) fMRI music perception dataset: 5 subjects, 540 15-s stimuli (GTZAN-derived selection: 480 training, 60 held-out test) with 10-embedding windows per clip as in the reference experiment; (2) Retrieval corpus: Free Music Archive large subset (~106,574 tracks) and a controlled small subset (~8,000 tracks); (3) Auxiliary evaluation set: held-out GTZAN clips and 60 clips for human rating. Preprocessing: standard fMRI preprocessing (motion correction, detrending, normalization), cortical surface registration, cortical voxel selection; compute MuLanmusic and MuLantext embeddings, w2v-BERT-avg, SoundStream-avg, wav2vec2 and HuBERT features per temporal window. Decoding pipeline: train voxel-wise regularized linear regressors (ridge) to predict each embedding dimension from training fMRI (five-fold CV for hyperparameters). Generate music by: (A) retrieval: nearest-neighbor in FMA using predicted embeddings (large and small corpora); (B) generation: condition MusicLM on averaged predicted MuLanmusic embeddings (and alternately on predicted MuLantext, wav2vec2, HuBERT). Baselines: random FMA sampling (chance), oracle retrieval (ground-truth MuLan embedding), retrieval conditioned on non-music embeddings, and generation conditioned on non-music embeddings. Encoding pipeline: voxel-wise prediction of fMRI responses from MuLanmusic, MuLantext, wav2vec2, HuBERT, melspectrogram using ridge regression and banded-ridge; estimate Pearson r and unique variance via variance partitioning. Evaluation metrics: (1) Identification accuracy: rank-based identification of target embedding among 60 candidates; (2) Cosine similarity between generated/retrieved audio embeddings and ground-truth embeddings (MuLan and w2v-BERT); (3) AudioSet top-n class agreement grouped by genre/instrument/mood; (4) Human perceptual semantic-match rating: N=20 raters, percentage correct identification and Likert similarity; (5) Encoding performance: Pearson r and explained variance per voxel and ROI (A1, STG); (6) BPM match percentage and vocal-gender classification accuracy; (7) Statistical tests: paired t-tests for method comparisons, permutation tests for voxel significance, FDR correction for multiple comparisons. Ablations and comparisons: (i) linear ridge vs MLP vs small Transformer for fMRI-to-embedding mapping; (ii) MuLanmusic vs MuLantext vs non-music embeddings as decoding targets; (iii) embedding temporal averaging vs windowed (no averaging) inputs; (iv) retrieval: large vs small FMA; (v) conditioning on combined high-level (MuLan) + low-level (SoundStream) embeddings vs high-level only; (vi) leave-one-genre-out generalization test. Experimental setup details: use identical train/test splits across comparisons, tune regularization per-dimension via nested CV, report mean±s.e.m. across subjects, enforce no subject-level mixing in training, and provide open code for replication. Risk Factors and Limitations: Technical failure modes: linear regressions may underfit complex brain-to-embedding mappings leading to poor predicted embeddings; generative model may not faithfully adhere to conditioning vectors or may collapse to dataset biases. Data and measurement constraints: fMRI temporal resolution and hemodynamic smoothing limit reconstruction of fine temporal structure; small subject sample size reduces generalizability and statistical power. Evaluation biases: embedding-space similarity and classifier-based metrics depend on embedding expressiveness and classifier calibration; human ratings are subjective and may be influenced by familiarity. Dataset and model biases: FMA and GTZAN cover limited genres and may introduce cultural or production biases; MuLan and MusicLM are proprietary and trained on corpora that may not match experimental stimuli. Scalability and compute: MusicLM conditioning and large-corpus retrieval require substantial compute and storage, limiting replication. Generalization limits: cross-subject variability and alignment issues impede direct subject-to-subject transfer; results may not extend to imagined music or to non-auditory semantic aspects. Interpretability limits: similarity in embedding space does not guarantee perceptual equivalence; mapping observed correspondences to specific cognitive processes remains ambiguous.
